estimate.damage_summary: A heavy bowl fell against a household display cabinet, cracking the cabinet-door glass and denting/gouging its solid-wood frame; a cabinet shelf is also reported scratched and chipped. The glass and timber damage are described as arising from the same sudden impact.
estimate.policy_notes: Sudden accidental damage can cover the cabinet’s non-glazing parts, subject to the schedule showing that peril as agreed; the claim description suggests it is intended to apply. Glass breakage and all associated glazing work are covered only if optional glazing is shown as agreed in the schedule, which was not provided. No deductible or sub-limit can be confirmed from the documents supplied.

lines.rationale: Drilling can qualify as preparatory glazing work if needed to receive the replacement pane or its hardware, but the invoice does not explain why it was necessary. Its coverage depends on the optional glazing peril being agreed.

lines.invoice_text: Installation of the new glass into the frame
lines.rationale: Refitting the replacement pane is a direct repair step for the cracked cabinet-door glass. It is covered only if optional glazing is agreed; one installation is plausible.

A pane made to fit the broken cabinet-door glazing is directly related, and one pane is supported by the description and photo. The pane is a glazing element, so accidental-damage cover alone does not insure it; optional glazing must be agreed.

lines.invoice_text: Repair of dented and gouged solid-wood door frame
lines.rationale: The reported impact damage to the cabinet’s non-glazing timber frame is a plausible sudden accidental loss; the photo visibly supports substantial gouging. A single localized repair and finish is reasonable, with the price allowing for careful colour matching.

lines.invoice_text: Repair and refinish of scratched and chipped wooden shelf
lines.rationale: The description attributes the shelf damage to the same impact, making localized repair potentially covered as sudden accidental damage. The shelf damage is less clearly verifiable in the photo, and only the damaged area—not general refinishing—would be reasonable.

One attendance charge is plausible for the undertaking’s visit to repair covered timber damage; the policy allows one attendance where indemnified work was carried out. A separate or repeat visit would not be payable without prior agreement.
